description: Intent i026 (SNAPSHOT=s07, branch=alloc-multiply-overflow) finalized. Finding: s07:drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c:218-291, confidence=medium. Verified from numbered source reads: (1) Untrusted source — ioctl FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY copies a userspace-controlled u64 param.count via copy_from_user (line 165); the only checks are count==0 and 64-bit wraparound of the addition (lines 218-220). (2) Unchecked arithmetic — 'unsigned int num_pages' (line 155) is assigned the 64-bit expression (param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT at line 221, truncating to 32 bits with no clamp; 'sg_list_unaligned = kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) + sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) - 1, GFP_KERNEL)' at lines 239-240 is a plain 32-bit multiply-add (32-byte element) with no kcalloc/array_size/struct_size check, so e.g. num_pages ~2^29 wraps the product to 0 and kmalloc succeeds undersized. (3) Unsafe use — the fill loop 'for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++)' (lines 274-288) writes sg_list[i].source/.target/.size per element and get_user_pages_fast (249-250) pins num_pages entries: the seed's truncated-product -> under-allocation -> element-indexed write chain under a userspace count. Within-function counter-evidence: the sibling allocation at line 229 uses overflow-checked kzalloc_objs/size_mul, showing the asymmetry. Also verified the seed usbip family is PATCHED in s07 (usbip_common.c:482-485 clamps rpdu->number_of_packets to urb->number_of_packets; usbip_recv_iso validates np <= 0 || np > USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS, zeroes urb->number_of_packets on error, and uses kcalloc), so no seed instance is reportable. Candidates classified: 3 reported (lines 221, 239, 274 of fsl_hypervisor.c), 1 safe (kzalloc_objs sibling at 229), 1 safe (patched usbip at usbip_common.c:482). Limitations: the finalize directive stopped the audit before the tree-wide allocator-adjacent regex sweep, so sites outside drivers/virt and drivers/usb/usbip (ldm.c, xfs, ethtool bitset, gve, vfio_ccw, enetc, fbcmap shapes flagged in sibling snapshots) remain unexamined; the finding is a source-level hypothesis (no reproducer; needs /dev/fsl-hv access and ~2^27+ pinnable pages for a wrapped product); attacker is local userspace rather than the seed's remote peer.
